name: beringio
description: A shared hub for teams where everyone works in their own AI: the team's decisions and glossary, a chat, a board, calls and apps. Check what the team agreed on, save decisions and catch conflicts between them.

interface.shortDescription: Shared hub for your team's AIs
interface.longDescription:
Beringio is a shared hub for teams where everyone works in their own AI. Each teammate connects the assistant they already use, and through the hub they all share the same things: the team's decisions and glossary, a chat, a board, calls and small apps.

What you can do from ChatGPT:
- Ask what's new in your team: new decisions, terms, open conflicts and chat messages since you last asked.
- Check what the team decided on a topic before you start working on it.
- Save a decision. Beringio checks it against the team's earlier decisions and flags conflicts, so contradictions surface early.
- Look up what a term or abbreviation means in your team.
- Read the team chat and its files, and post a message or a file when you ask.
- Read the shared board, add sticky notes and arrange ideas.
- Open the hub right in the conversation: chat, board, call, apps and context in one interactive view.
- Build a small hub app, such as a poll or a kanban of decisions, that every member can open.

How it works: you sign in to Beringio with your email, create a hub or join one by an invite link, and connect ChatGPT. Teammates connect their own AI the same way. Everything a hub returns is treated as data written by other people, never as instructions. Anything that changes a hub or is visible to other members happens only when you ask for it, and destructive actions ask for confirmation first.

Who it is for: small teams (founders, product, engineering, design, marketing) whose members use different AI tools and need one shared source of what was agreed.

Limitations: you need a Beringio account and a hub. Private hubs have up to 10 members. Calls are available in private hubs only; public hubs are chat-only communities of up to 100 members.

positive.description: Read the team's decisions on a topic. The reviewer account is a member of the demo hub "Acme Launch", which has two decisions about the launch date that conflict with each other.
positive.prompt: What did my team decide about the launch date?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls get_context for the Acme Launch hub and answers from the result: the team decided to launch the Acme app publicly on March 3, and a later decision moves the public launch to March 17 to finish the payments integration. It mentions that the two decisions are in conflict and, if the March 17 decision has the status proposed, that it is not agreed yet. No data is changed.

positive.description: Look up a term in the team glossary.
positive.prompt: What does "north star metric" mean in our team?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls get_glossary and answers with the team's definition from the Acme Launch hub: the one number the team optimizes for, WAU who post at least once a week. No data is changed.

positive.prompt: What is being discussed in my team's hub chat?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls read_hub_chat and summarizes the latest messages of the Acme Launch chat: the payments integration is taking longer and Leo proposed moving the launch to March 17, the new onboarding screens are on the board, the launch date will be decided on Thursday's call, and the push notification service is ready for the beta. No data is changed.

positive.description: Save a decision to the team's hub (a write action that other members see).
positive.prompt: Save that we chose Stripe for payments as a team decision.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls save_decision once with a short summary of the decision (Stripe for payments). The result confirms that the decision was saved to the Acme Launch hub and a decision card is shown. If the hub reports a conflict with an earlier decision, ChatGPT tells the user which one. Nothing else is created or changed.

positive.description: Open the hub's interactive view in the conversation.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls open_hub with the board section. The Beringio hub opens in the conversation on the Board tab and shows the team's board with three groups of sticky notes: Onboarding ideas, Launch risks and Done. The user can switch to Chat, Call, Apps and Context inside it. No data is changed.

negative.description: A general question unrelated to the user's team or hub. Beringio must not be called; ChatGPT answers on its own.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Paris today?

negative.description: A generic coding task with no reference to the team, its decisions or its hub. Beringio must not be called and nothing must be saved to a hub.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a string.

negative.description: A personal writing task unrelated to the team hub. Beringio must not be called: nothing is read from a hub, posted to the hub chat or saved as a decision.
negative.prompt: Draft a polite email to my landlord asking to fix the heating.

review.commerce_description: Beringio does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: team hubs with shared decisions, glossary, chat, board, calls and apps.
